title: Session-presets personalization sketch
content:
Quick brain-dump: session-aware presets for personalization (sketchy PRD / experiment plan)

SUMMARY
- Idea: give app developers a lightweight way to attach "presets" to a user session that influence model behavior (temperature, system prompt fragments, safety filters, response format hints, reranking weights, etc.) without requiring full model fine-tuning or new endpoints.
- Presets stored server-side (Redwood) or client-provided token; applied at runtime with explicit precedence rules.
- Main value: faster iteration on personalization, cheaper than per-user models, enables safer scoped behavioral tweaks, and allows consistent A/Bing and rollout.

WHY NOW
- Customers repeatedly ask for per-user behavior controls (engineering/solutions calls last qtr).
- We have caching + routing infra to key by session metadata, so adding a small config layer is low-risk.
- Opens up paid features for Dedicated/Private (preset storage & longer TTLs).

PROBLEM STATEMENT / USER JOBS
- Product engineers want to: 1) bias responses toward a persona or tone, 2) pin deterministic schema outputs, 3) toggle safety or hallucination penalties per customer or route, 4) experiment with prompt fragments without modifying model config.
- Constraints: minimal latency impact, auditable changes, rollbackable, low overhead for infra and UX.

GOALS (success metrics)
- Experiment: 1) <10ms median added latency on request path; 2) 80% of early adopters can reach desired tone match in <=3 iterations; 3) no increase in safety incidents in pilot customers.
- Business: feature adoption by 10 pilot teams in 6 weeks => bump in Dedicated interest.

NON-GOALS
- Not replacing model-level personalization (fine-tuning, LoRA).
- Not full feature flag system — simple per-session config only.

PROPOSED PRODUCT / ARCHITECTURE
- Preset object (JSON) fields: id, display_name, owner_team, ttl_seconds, precedence_rank, system_prompt_fragments (list), runtime_overrides { temperature, top_p, max_tokens }, post_processing_hooks (rerank: weight, safety: level), allowed_routes (list), audit_metadata.
- Storage: short-term presets live in in-memory config cache (per-region), persisted in customer-scoped metadata store (encrypted). Private deploy: option to keep presets in customer DB via connector.
- Application: API adds optional header X-Redwood-Preset: preset-id | <base64 small JSON>. On request, runtime resolves preset -> merges with route config -> logs applied keys to trace.
- Caching: key by (preset-id, model, route) to reuse compiled kernel selections and cache warmups.

API SKETCH (very rough)
- Create preset: POST /v1/presets { name, fragments: [...], overrides: {...}, ttl } -> returns id
- Apply (client): include header X-Redwood-Preset: preset_id OR X-Redwood-Preset-Blob: <base64 json>
- Admin: GET /v1/presets?team=...; POST /v1/presets/:id/rollout -> can pin to environment or do canary percent

UX IDEAS (console)
- Preset editor: side-by-side live playground (input prompt -> model output) with a slider for temperature and checkboxes for safety levels.
- Quick presets gallery: "Casual", "Enterprise-Precise", "Elide-PHI" templates.
- Audit view: timeline of changes, who pushed which preset and which requests applied it (links to traces).

USER STORIES
- As a product engineer, I can create a preset for my beta users so they get friendlier tone without changing other users.
- As an SRE, I can see which presets are hot and evict or pin them to avoid memory thrash.
- As a compliance officer, I can require "elide-PHI" preset be applied for routes handling PII.

METRICS / OBSERVABILITY
- Adoption: count of presets created / active per week; presets applied per route.
- Perf: added latency distribution, cache hit ratio for preset-keyed caches.
- Quality: small eval set per preset (prompt set) -> BLEU/ROUGE/approx match to target tone vector; manual labels for safety regressions.

RISKS / EDGE CASES
- Preset abuse: customers pack arbitrary system prompts to bypass safety filters — need enforcement layer (denylist, length limits).
- Explosive combinatorics: multi-presets or nested fragments may create unexpected behaviors; start with single preset per request.
- Storage bloat for long-lived presets — policy for TTL and cleanup.

EXPERIMENT PLAN (pilot)
- Phase 0: internal dogfood -> product analytics + ops team. 2 weeks.
- Phase 1: invite 3 pilot customers (GTM and CS coordinated). Provide UI + API. 4 weeks.
- Phase 2: iterate based on feedback + broaden to 30 internal teams. Monitor safety metrics. 6 weeks.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOS
- Precedence: how does preset merge with route defaults and per-call overrides? (suggestion: call overrides > preset > route > model defaults). Need to spell out merge rules precisely.
- Security: what patterns for preventing cross-tenant leak in hosted mode? Need IAM/policy check at apply-time.
- Billing: feature behind Dedicated+Private? Or hosted tier + usage? prototype pricing options.
- UX: allow temp local "ad-hoc" blobs in header for quick testing vs persisted presets. How long should ad-hoc be allowed?

NEXT STEPS (me)
- Draft short internal RFC for infra feasibility (ping infra & runtime).
- Prototype header merge in local dev: runtime hook to read header and inject system fragment; measure latency. (owner: Owen)
- Sketch console wireframes + playground (owner: Maya).
- Sync with security for policy enforcement rules (owner: Kai).
- Slack thread: #prod-presets -> create and tag stakeholders.

NOTES TO SELF
- Keep design simple first: single preset per-request, strict size limits, server-validated JSON.
- Followup: check related requests in support logs for requests asking for "tone" or "strict-format" customization.
